# 2 Baruch Chapter 32 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**32:1** For whatever-is-now is-nothing; but-whatever-is-coming will-be-great. For everything-that-is-corruptible will-pass-away, and-everything-that-dies will-depart, and-every-present-time will-be-forgotten, and-there-will-be-no-remembrance-of-the-present-[age], because-the-coming-one comes quickly.

**32:2** For-the-souls-of-the-righteous who-are-now in-distress know what-has-been-prepared for-them, and-on-account-of-it they-will-not-be-distressed.

**32:3** But-as-for-us — if-we-did-not-know that-we-are-in-distress, we-would-have-understood nothing; for-we-know that-distress-of-the-world [will not last].

**32:4** And-I-said to-them-furthermore: Will-not-all-these-[distresses] pass-away from-us? And-will-not-a-time-of-rest-come for-us? And-behold, Zion, she-shall-be-built-up again, and-the-offering-[sacrifices] will-be-restored, and-the-priests-will-return to-their-place, and-the-peoples-will-return to-the-land.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Syriac Codex Ambrosianus. Baruch continues exhorting the people. The promise of Zion's rebuilding (v.4) is explicitly temporal — a rebuilt Zion before the end, not the final eschatological city. This distinguishes 2 Baruch's complex theology of two destructions and two rebuildings.*
